claim: node_exporter uses a static factory-map registry: collector/collector.go declares factories = make(map[string]func(...) (Collector, error)) and registerCollector(name, isDefaultEnabled, factory) writes into it; each collector file self-registers from its own func init().
design_impact: Direct prior art for the Fixed Registry default: registry is built at program start from explicit per-file init() calls, no reflection, no runtime discovery. Adopt the shape; prefer explicit Register(check) over init() magic for reviewability.

claim: node_exporter's Collector isolation is only against RETURNED ERRORS: execute() logs the error and sets success=0. It has no recover() and no per-collector context deadline; collectors run concurrently via an unbounded goroutine+WaitGroup fan-out.
design_impact: The most-cited prior art does NOT satisfy our E-rules. Per-check panic recovery and per-check deadlines are our own addition, not something to copy. Do not cite node_exporter as evidence that error-return isolation is sufficient.

claim: node_exporter defines a sentinel var ErrNoData = errors.New("collector returned no data") plus IsNoDataError(), separating 'ran fine, nothing to report' from a real failure.
design_impact: Precedent for a tri-state result: our UNKNOWN-with-reason is the same idea, and must never be collapsed into FAIL.

claim: ghw is organised as one package per hardware domain under pkg/ (block, cpu, memory, baseboard, bios, chassis, product, net, pci, topology, ...), each exposing a *Info struct and a discovery function.
design_impact: Supports a per-domain split of machine description (internal/machine/{dmi,cpu,mem,block,os}) rather than one monolith; keeps unknown-handling local to each domain.

claim: ghw exposes a PRODUCTION fs-root override: option.WithChroot(dir) plus the GHW_CHROOT environment variable read by EnvOrDefaultChroot().
design_impact: Named anti-pattern. Any ambient env-var root override is a safety hole for a posture sensor (an attacker-controlled env var redirects every read and every finding). Our root seam must be unexported and test-only.

claim: ghw's linuxdmi.Item() logs a warning and returns the explicit sentinel util.UNKNOWN = "unknown" when a DMI sysfs file cannot be read (the root-only case), rather than returning an empty string.
design_impact: Independent industry confirmation of B6/EACCES-is-not-absent: a permission error yields an explicit unknown, never "". We go further and attach the errno as evidence.

claim: gopsutil bakes HOST_PROC / HOST_SYS / HOST_ETC environment overrides into the library itself (internal/common.GetEnv + HostProc/HostSys/HostEtc).
design_impact: Second named anti-pattern, and a concrete reason to REJECT gopsutil as a dependency for a security sensor: its read root is silently redirectable by inherited environment.

claim: osquery-go registers tables statically as data: table.NewPlugin(name, []ColumnDefinition, GenerateFunc) with typed column metadata structs.
design_impact: Confirms 'static registry of {id, typed metadata, run func}' is the norm for this software class; supports a []Check literal or Register() list over any dynamic plugin mechanism.

claim: kube-bench separates check DEFINITIONS (YAML: id, text, audit, tests, remediation, scored) from the Go RUNNER (check.Check struct with a State result field).
design_impact: Metadata-as-data is right; externalising it to YAML is not, at 2-4k LOC. Keep check metadata as Go struct literals colocated with the check body; a YAML DSL would add a parser, a schema and a failure mode for zero benefit.

claim: go.dev/doc/modules/layout is the official Go guidance and endorses internal/ for supporting packages and cmd/ for commands; golang-standards/project-layout's own README states verbatim that it is NOT an official standard defined by the core Go dev team.
design_impact: Use cmd/sensor + internal/*; do not adopt the pkg//api//configs/ scaffolding of golang-standards, which is aimed at large multi-binary repos.

claim: exec.CommandContext's default Cancel is cmd.Cancel = func() error { return cmd.Process.Kill() } (os/exec source), and os.Process.Kill documents 'This only kills the Process itself, not any other processes it may have started.' Setting SysProcAttr.Setpgid alone therefore does NOT give group kill.
design_impact: The bounded runner must set cmd.Cancel itself to syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, SIGKILL). This is the single highest-value correctness fact in the exec design.

claim: Cmd.WaitDelay (Go 1.20+) bounds two delays in Wait: a child that fails to exit after the Context is canceled, and a child that exits but leaves I/O pipes unclosed; on expiry the parent's pipe fds are force-closed and Wait returns exec.ErrWaitDelay ("exec: WaitDelay expired before I/O complete").
design_impact: WaitDelay is mandatory, not optional: it is the only stdlib guarantee that Wait returns. Map ErrWaitDelay to observation status TIMEOUT (never to a false/pass verdict).

claim: LOCAL_REPRO: with a 3s context and no WaitDelay, `sh -c 'sleep 30 & echo parent-done; exit 0'` made cmd.Output() block for 30.01s — the context deadline fired and the leader was already dead, but Wait stayed blocked on the pipe held by the orphaned grandchild. With WaitDelay=200ms the same command returned in 0.21s with exec.ErrWaitDelay and the 12 bytes of output still captured.
design_impact: Empirical proof that a per-check context deadline alone does not bound a check. Partial output before the cap/timeout is still usable as evidence.

claim: LOCAL_REPRO (novel): WaitDelay bounds OUR wait but does not clean up the host. After a 300ms context timeout on `sh -c 'sleep 2001 | cat'` with WaitDelay=200ms and the default Cancel, the `sleep 2001` grandchild was still running (pgrep count 1). With Setpgid:true plus cmd.Cancel doing syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL), zero survivors remained.
design_impact: Leaving stray processes on a customer's production host violates the read-only/no-side-effects invariant. Setpgid + negative-PID kill is required for hygiene even where WaitDelay already prevents our own hang. Both are needed; neither substitutes for the other.

claim: Stdlib syscall on linux/amd64 provides everything the bounded runner needs: SysProcAttr{Setpgid bool, Pgid int}, Kill(pid int, sig Signal), SIGKILL. golang.org/x/sys is not required for process-group kill.
design_impact: Zero-dependency bounded exec. Note the Windows trap: `go doc syscall.SysProcAttr` on the authoring workstation shows the Windows struct; always cross-doc with GOOS=linux.

claim: os/exec documents that Wait closes the StdoutPipe after the command exits, so 'it is thus incorrect to call Wait before all reads from the pipe have completed' and incorrect to call Run when using StdoutPipe. Assigning cmd.Stdout to a capped io.Writer instead lets os/exec own the copy goroutine and its WaitDelay interaction.
design_impact: Cap output with a limiting io.Writer assigned to cmd.Stdout/cmd.Stderr before Start; do not hand-roll StdoutPipe + LimitReader. cmd.Output() is rejected because it is uncapped.

claim: The WaitDelay pipe-close behaviour exists specifically to address golang/go#23019, which is cited by URL inside os/exec source; the design landed via accepted proposal golang/go#50436 (milestone Go1.20). golang/go#57140, sometimes cited in this context, is unrelated (x/exp darwin build failure).
design_impact: Cite #23019 and #50436 in the implementation prompt; do not cite #57140. Any blog that omits Cancel/WaitDelay is pre-1.20 and must not be used as a pattern source.

claim: inode(7) states pseudofile st_size is not accurate — 0 for many /proc files, 4096 for many /sys files; kernel Documentation/filesystems/sysfs.rst states the sysfs read buffer is always PAGE_SIZE (4096 on x86). LOCAL_REPRO confirmed /proc/meminfo, /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/self/status all report st_size=0 while /sys/devices/system/cpu/online reports 4096.
design_impact: Never size a buffer from Stat, never treat size 0 as an empty file, and never treat 4096 as the real length of a sysfs attribute. Read to EOF against an explicit cap.

claim: os.ReadFile handles size-0 pseudofiles correctly by design — its source comments name /proc explicitly ('files in Linux's /proc claim size 0 but then do not work right if read in small pieces') and it grows the buffer until EOF — but it is UNBOUNDED. LOCAL_REPRO: os.ReadFile(/proc/meminfo)=1503 bytes, os.ReadFile(/proc/cpuinfo)=16830 bytes despite st_size=0.
design_impact: os.ReadFile is correct but unsafe as the sensor's primitive: a large or streaming node (/proc/kcore, an unexpected device) would grow until OOM. Use a bounded reader everywhere; keep os.ReadFile only for fixed small sysfs attributes if at all.

claim: LOCAL_REPRO: opening with O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK, rejecting non-regular files by Fstat, then io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, cap+1)) reads /proc/cpuinfo to exactly cap=200 bytes and flags truncated=true. The same helper rejects /dev/null and /dev/zero with 'not a regular file: Dcrw-rw-rw-'.
design_impact: This is the sensor's canonical read primitive: cap+1 read to detect truncation, mode gate on the OPEN FD (not on a pre-open Lstat) to close the TOCTOU window, O_NONBLOCK so a FIFO cannot block.

claim: LOCAL_REPRO: /sys/block contains 28 entries, 28 of which are symlinks (0 non-symlink entries). Every block device is reached through a relative symlink such as loop0 -> ../devices/virtual/block/loop0.
design_impact: A blanket O_NOFOLLOW or 'refuse symlinks' policy would make block-device enumeration return zero devices. The symlink policy must be path-scoped: follow inside /sys and /proc, refuse in user-writable paths (/home, /tmp, /var/tmp), and never follow while walking for secrets.

claim: os.Root (Go 1.24; ReadFile/Readlink added 1.25) performs openat-per-component within a directory and rejects paths that escape it, including via symlinks. LOCAL_REPRO on Go 1.26.2: os.OpenRoot("/sys").ReadFile("block/loop0/size") succeeded (following the relative ../devices/... symlink inside the root), while Open("../etc/passwd") failed with 'path escapes from parent'.
design_impact: os.Root("/sys") and os.Root("/proc") are the right production primitives: they give sysfs symlink traversal AND kernel-enforced escape prevention with no TOCTOU gap, at zero dependency cost. Root.FS() also yields the test seam for free.

claim: LOCAL_REPRO resolving an open question from the source survey: os.Root does work on /proc and its magic symlinks — os.OpenRoot("/proc").ReadFile("self/status") returned 1467 bytes on Go 1.26.2 / kernel 6.18 WSL2. Reading through another process's magic root symlink ("1/root/etc/passwd") failed with ENOTDIR as an unprivileged user rather than being silently followed.
design_impact: Removes the last objection to using os.Root for /proc. Caveat recorded: verified on kernel 6.18 WSL2, not on the target's 6.8/7.0 bare metal — behaviour depends on openat2 support, present since 5.6, so drift is unlikely but the sensor must degrade to plain reads if OpenRoot returns an error.

claim: LOCAL_REPRO: os.Open on a FIFO blocked for the full 700ms observation window (never returned), while os.OpenFile with O_RDONLY|syscall.O_NONBLOCK returned immediately with no error; Lstat reported mode prw------- with ModeNamedPipe set. Matches fifo(7)/open(2).
design_impact: An unbounded open() is itself a hang risk, before any read. O_NONBLOCK on every open is a hard rule for the sensor, in addition to the mode gate.

claim: syscall.Stat_t.Dev exists in stdlib on linux/amd64 and is reachable via fi.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t). LOCAL_REPRO showed distinct Dev values per mount (/=2096, /proc=61, /sys=24, /dev=6, /run=63, /tmp=71), so Dev comparison implements xdev.
design_impact: Bounded walks stay on one filesystem by capturing the root's Dev and skipping any entry whose Dev differs — no dependency, no /proc/self/mountinfo parsing needed. Caveat: bind mounts and btrfs subvolumes make Dev a mount-view identity, not a physical-device identity.

claim: Stdlib syscall on linux declares Getxattr, Listxattr, Setxattr, Removexattr and Statfs with Statfs_t{Type, Flags, ...}. LOCAL_REPRO on Go 1.26.2: syscall.Getxattr(path, "system.posix_acl_access", buf) returned ENODATA for files without an ACL, syscall.Listxattr returned n=0, syscall.Statfs("/") returned Type=0xef53 (EXT2_SUPER_MAGIC/ext4) Flags=0x1020.
design_impact: ACL presence, xattr listing and mount-flag reads (nosuid/nodev/noexec via Statfs Flags) are all available with zero dependencies. ENODATA is the correct 'no ACL present' signal and must be distinguished from EACCES and EOPNOTSUPP.

claim: The system.posix_acl_access wire format is fixed by kernel uapi: a 4-byte little-endian header (POSIX_ACL_XATTR_VERSION 0x0002) followed by 8-byte entries {__le16 e_tag, __le16 e_perm, __le32 e_id}. No maintained Go library decodes it: pkg/xattr (active) only returns raw bytes, joshlf/go-acl has not been pushed since 2020-04-11 and has no releases.
design_impact: BUILD a ~50-line decoder over stdlib syscall.Getxattr. Directly serves BMC_INBAND_ACCESS 'who may open /dev/ipmi0' on a host where getfacl is absent.

claim: CONTESTED, resolved: the common claim that stdlib syscall is 'deprecated, use x/sys' overstates the source. src/syscall/syscall.go carries a NOTE recommending golang.org/x/sys for most new code, but no individual symbol carries a godoc Deprecated: tag and the package is frozen, not scheduled for removal. Every symbol this sensor needs (Setpgid, Kill, SIGKILL, Stat_t.Dev, Getxattr, Listxattr, Statfs/Statfs_t) is present in stdlib syscall on linux/amd64 and was exercised in LOCAL_REPRO.
design_impact: Position A (x/sys is required because syscall is deprecated) is rejected on source evidence. Position B (stdlib suffices) is adopted for a single-GOOS/GOARCH deliverable: zero dependencies, nothing to vendor, nothing to audit. Reversal condition: needing a syscall or struct field absent from frozen stdlib (e.g. statx, openat2 flags, RTNETLINK), at which point x/sys becomes justified and should be added as the ONLY dependency.

claim: filepath.WalkDir does not follow symbolic links and avoids the per-entry os.Lstat that filepath.Walk performs; fs.SkipDir prunes the current directory and fs.SkipAll (Go 1.20) aborts the whole walk. WalkDir has no built-in timeout or entry budget.
design_impact: Use WalkDir with an enclosing budget struct: depth cap, entry-count cap, deadline check, xdev check and a prune list; return SkipDir on prune and SkipAll on budget exhaustion, and record 'budget exhausted' as evidence so absence is never inferred from an aborted walk.

claim: encoding/json sorts map keys and emits struct fields in declaration order. LOCAL_REPRO confirmed: a map literal {z,a,m} marshalled as {"a","m","z"} while the struct's declared field order (path, attrs, note) was preserved.
design_impact: Deterministic output needs no third-party canonical-JSON library: define output structs in the intended order, use map[string]string/any for open evidence bags, and sort slices (findings by category then check_id) explicitly.

claim: LOCAL_REPRO: json.Marshal escaped < > & as \u003c \u003e \u0026; json.NewEncoder with SetEscapeHTML(false) emitted them literally, and Encoder.Encode appended a trailing newline.
design_impact: Use json.Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false) and SetIndent("", "  ") so evidence strings containing shell/config text stay human-readable in findings.json. Account for the trailing newline when hashing output.

claim: LOCAL_REPRO: json.Marshal of a time.Time produced "2026-09-09T01:02:03.456Z" — RFC3339Nano trims trailing zeros, so the rendered width varies with the fractional value.
design_impact: Do not marshal time.Time directly for collected_at. Format explicitly with t.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339) into a string field so two runs differ only by the timestamp value, never by field width or precision.

claim: LOCAL_REPRO: GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build on Windows with Go 1.26.2 produced 'ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64 ... statically linked'; under WSL Ubuntu 26.04 ldd reported 'not a dynamic executable' and all four repro binaries ran as uid 1000.
design_impact: The Windows->linux/amd64 static cross-build is proven end to end on this workstation, which is the only build path available given `go` is UTILITY_MISSING on the target. No glibc dependency, so Ubuntu 24.04 on the target is not a constraint.

claim: With cgo unavailable (CGO_ENABLED=0) os/user uses its pure-Go implementation that parses /etc/passwd and /etc/group directly, and net uses the pure-Go resolver.
design_impact: user.Lookup on the target will see local files only. Harmless here (nsswitch on the host is files-only) but must be stated as evidence provenance: our user/group findings are '/etc/passwd as parsed by the pure-Go resolver', not NSS. Generic hosts with LDAP/SSSD would need this caveat in the finding.

claim: cmd/go supports -trimpath (removes filesystem paths from the binary) and -buildvcs (stamps VCS info); runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo exposes that stamp at runtime via BuildInfo.Settings keys such as vcs.revision, and `go version -m <binary>` prints it offline.
design_impact: --version comes from ReadBuildInfo with a -ldflags -X fallback for the semantic version; -trimpath prevents leaking C:\lava-sensor-exercise\... paths into a binary shipped to a customer.

claim: Windows filesystems carry no POSIX execute bit, so a tar built from a Windows working copy records whatever mode the Windows stat emulation reports for the binary.
design_impact: Build the tarball with an explicit header mode (tar --mode=0755 for the binary, or hdr.Mode=0o755 with archive/tar) AND document chmod +x as a fallback in the run instructions. A non-executable binary is the single cheapest way to fail A2 ('if we cannot run it, we cannot give you credit').

claim: flag.NewFlagSet plus a switch on os.Args[1] is the stdlib subcommand pattern; flag.ExitOnError makes an unparsable flag call os.Exit(2) and -h/-help exit 0.
design_impact: ~20 lines of stdlib covers `sensor scan --out ...`, `sensor --version`, `sensor help`. No CLI framework.

claim: Scanner tools that conflate 'findings exist' with 'process failed' (trivy's --exit-code) are a documented usability wart; sysexits.h reserves 64 for usage errors.
design_impact: Exit policy: 0 = scan completed and findings.json written (regardless of pass/fail/unknown counts); 1 = scan could not complete or could not write the output; 2 = CLI usage error (matches flag's default). Never make exit status depend on finding severity.

claim: spf13/cobra's go.mod requires four external modules (go-md2man/v2, mousetrap, pflag, yaml/v3) for man-page generation, Windows mouse-trap handling, POSIX flags and YAML.
design_impact: REJECT cobra/urfave/kong for a one-subcommand binary: four dependencies and a YAML parser inside a security sensor's supply chain buys nothing the stdlib flag package does not already do.

claim: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh implements the SSH protocol (client and server) and configures its server via a programmatic ServerConfig struct; it contains no parser for the sshd_config file format.
design_impact: No reuse available from the closest-looking stdlib-adjacent package. Also note: pulling x/crypto for a parser it does not have would add a large dependency for nothing.

claim: github.com/kevinburke/ssh_config parses CLIENT ssh_config (Host alias blocks, Get(alias, key)); its own documentation notes the Match directive is unsupported.
design_impact: REJECT: pointing a client-config parser at sshd_config would misapply Host-block semantics to a file whose scoping rules are Match-based, producing confidently wrong findings — worse than no parser.

claim: A survey of the Go ecosystem (k0sproject/rig sshconfig, ericwq/ssh_config, shuLhan/share, petems/go-sshconfig, mikkeloscar/sshconfig, kevinburke/ssh_config) found no maintained sshd_config (server-side) parser; all target client config.
design_impact: BUILD a minimal sshd_config reader restricted to the directives the checks need. Negative claim from a non-exhaustive survey: re-verify once at implementation time before writing the parser.

claim: sshd_config(5) specifies: 'Unless noted otherwise, for each keyword, the first obtained value will be used'; Include files are glob-expanded and processed in lexical order; and directives inside a Match block apply only when its criteria are satisfied, with only the first instance of a keyword among satisfied Match blocks applied.
design_impact: Indicts naive grep three ways: grep reports last or all matches where sshd takes the first; grep counts directives inside unsatisfied Match blocks as global; grep on one file misses Include drop-ins that can win. On the target this is live, not theoretical: the first line of sshd_config is Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf and 00-latitude-instant-deploy.conf restates PasswordAuthentication.

claim: testing/fstest.MapFS is an in-memory fs.FS keyed by path, and symlink entries (ModeSymlink with the target in Data, plus ReadLink/ReadLinkFS) are supported in current Go.
design_impact: MapFS can model a fake sysfs including its symlinks, but since 28/28 /sys/block entries are symlinks this must be proven by one unit test in the implementation rather than assumed; the fallback is a real fixture tree under testdata/ built by the test with os.Symlink.

claim: os.DirFS documents that it is not a chroot-style security mechanism — a symlink under the prefix pointing outside it is still followed — and directs callers to Root.FS for escape prevention.
design_impact: os.DirFS is acceptable for trusted testdata fixtures only. Production reads use os.Root; the test seam is an fs.FS parameter that receives Root.FS() in production and a fixture FS in tests.

claim: The go tool ignores directories named testdata (and names starting with . or _) when matching packages.
design_impact: Fixture trees and golden files live under testdata/ next to the package; they are never compiled into the shipped binary.

claim: The flag-gated golden-file update idiom (var update = flag.Bool("update", false, ...); go test -update) is a de facto Go convention rather than a stdlib feature.
design_impact: Adopt it for the findings.json golden test, but keep the golden file reviewed by a human: a blanket -update run is how a regression gets blessed.

claim: testing/synctest (GA in Go 1.25; the Go 1.24 GOEXPERIMENT API was removed in 1.26) virtualises time for goroutines blocked inside a bubble; it is aimed at concurrency tests, not at stamping a fixed timestamp into output.
design_impact: Do not reach for synctest. Inject a now func() time.Time into the runner; the fake returns a fixed instant so golden files are byte-stable. Never reference GOEXPERIMENT=synctest, which no longer exists in 1.26.

claim: testing.T.Setenv calls os.Setenv for the whole process and therefore cannot be used in parallel tests or tests with parallel ancestors.
design_impact: PATH-shim fault injection (simulating a missing or slow utility) forces those tests to be non-parallel. Prefer injecting the exec runner interface over manipulating PATH wherever the check allows it.

claim: LOCAL_REPRO gap: setfacl is absent in the local WSL image, so the POSIX ACL decoder path was exercised only to the ENODATA (no-ACL) branch; the entry-decoding loop against real ACL bytes is UNVERIFIED locally.
design_impact: The ACL decoder needs a unit test with a hand-built byte fixture (header 02 00 00 00 + entries) rather than a live setfacl round-trip, and the check must report UNKNOWN with the raw byte length as evidence if the version field is not 2.

claim: task/original/finding.schema.json is not present in the repository at research time (task/original contains only the HTML and PDF brief).
design_impact: Schema-shape decisions stay deferred; the validation STRATEGY (embed + validate before write) is decidable without the file and is what this track recommends. Filed as R5-OR1.

claim: Independent Bowtie conformance data (report-history NDJSON, run started 2026-09-08, pass rates recomputed from the raw run rather than read off a badge) shows santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema v6.0.2 at 100% on draft 2020-12 (1301/1301), 2019-09 (1261/1261) and draft-07 (929/929); xeipuuv/gojsonschema v1.2.0 scores 874/929 (94.1%) on draft-07 with 20 hard errors and is not registered for 2019-09 or 2020-12 at all.
design_impact: Library selection is decided on measured conformance, not README claims. santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 is the pick; xeipuuv is disqualified on both draft coverage and correctness.

claim: Only two Go implementations have Bowtie harnesses at all (santhosh-tekuri v6 and xeipuuv). kaptinlin/jsonschema and qri-io/jsonschema have no harness, so their 2020-12 claims are self-reported and unverified.
design_impact: Treat kaptinlin as a fallback only, and only after running the official JSON-Schema-Test-Suite against it ourselves. Never accept a README draft-support claim as evidence.

claim: santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema v6.0.3 (released 2026-08-06) has one production dependency, golang.org/x/text (dlclark/regexp2 is test-only); v5 has none but is frozen. kaptinlin/jsonschema pulls goccy/go-yaml, google/uuid, kaptinlin/go-i18n, kaptinlin/jsonpointer plus transitives and requires go 1.27. qri-io/jsonschema last had a real commit 2024-12-18 with 42 open issues including $ref bugs; xeipuuv last had a real commit 2020-10-27 with 144 open issues.
design_impact: REUSE santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 as the sensor's single third-party dependency. One x/text transitive is acceptable; a YAML parser and an i18n stack inside a security sensor's supply chain is not. A go 1.27 directive would also break the pinned toolchain.

claim: omissis/go-jsonschema (formerly atombender) generates Go types from a schema at build time, which requires the schema to be fixed at compile time. Lava supplies finding.schema.json as the contract artifact and it is not yet in hand.
design_impact: Codegen is disqualified as the validation strategy, but remains a legitimate optional extra once the real schema arrives: generate types to catch drift at compile time AND validate at runtime. Do not substitute codegen for runtime validation.

claim: encoding/json/v2 is still experimental and opt-in behind GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 as of Go 1.26 (the Go 1.26 release notes do not mention it at all), and the official v1-to-v2 migration notes state that a Go map marshals in deterministic order in v1 but in NON-deterministic order in v2 unless the Deterministic option is set.
design_impact: Ship on encoding/json v1 with no GOEXPERIMENT flags. This is a hard constraint, not a preference: adopting v2 would silently break the deterministic-output requirement (D8) for exactly the evidence maps the findings file is made of.

claim: encoding/json formats floats as if by ES6 number-to-string conversion using strconv.AppendFloat with precision -1 (shortest round-trip), which is deterministic per value but can render exponent forms for large magnitudes.
design_impact: Use int64 for every byte count, size, mode, uid/gid, exit code and duration-in-milliseconds in the findings document; reserve floats for nothing.

claim: Runtime validation of the marshalled document against the embedded schema, immediately before writing findings.json, is the only strategy that protects the delivered artifact; test-time-only validation protects fixtures the grader may never run.
design_impact: go:embed the schema, compile once at startup, validate the final document before the write, and on failure write nothing to --out, print the failing instance pointers to stderr and exit 1. Keep the same validation in a golden test so the failure is caught in development first.
